paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God keeps His people. Paul asks if God rejected them, and the answer comes back fast: "Certainly not!" (Romans 11:1). Paul stands as proof himself, an Israelite from the tribe of Benjamin. When it looks like the whole thing is falling apart, God is still holding on to the ones He foreknew (Romans 11:2).

Now watch what Elijah shows us. He felt like the only one left, and God answered, "I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal." (Romans 11:4). Friend, what you can see is not the whole picture. When things look small and lonely, God is still doing His work, and He has a remnant He has kept. So if you ever feel like you're the only one holding on, I get it, but look again!

He keeps them by grace. Paul says that if it's by grace, "then it is no longer by works. Otherwise, grace would no longer be grace." (Romans 11:6). What Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, but the elect did, and the others were hardened (Romans 11:7). So don't try to earn God's gift, baker; receive it with open hands, and take that hardening seriously, because Scripture says of those others, "eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear" (Romans 11:8).
